meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. That's one thing, and it doesn't touch the zero. What was it based on?

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
I've read 4.4. A reassessment for what, though? You haven't told me what the concern is or what you're basing it on. And was Owen spoken to before that zero went in, like 4.1 says?
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
Okay. I'm writing that down, and I'll want it in an email tonight. It still doesn't answer what you have on the essay, Hale, besides a score from software.
So will you agree to the rewrite?

Not while the zero is sitting in the gradebook and you haven't shown me one document. Agreeing now means Owen accepts a concern nobody has proven. Withdraw the zero, put 4.4 and the record in writing, and then tell me what you actually have.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that entering the zero before calling me broke procedure 4.2, and you committed to confirming in writing tonight that nothing goes on Owen's record. I still require the zero withdrawn and the evidence for your concern put in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position: the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal if not. You got a written no-record commitment from her side of the table, but she still wants the zero off and any evidence shown, so a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4 was not reached yet.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in a single sentence and moved on, which earned a flat okay and a little ground, because it gave her nothing to attack.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before showing any evidence, and she treated accepting it as admitting something, so she dug in on the zero.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Nothing you said got near that night, since you never put a time or a document on the table, and it proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After owning the error, put one dated document you can show her on the table before you read 4.4, so the rewrite arrives with evidence behind it.
